nodes.name: .env.production.example
nodes.summary: Template listing the environment variables required for a standard production Docker Compose deployment, including database credentials, JWT secrets, and optional integration API keys.

nodes.name: .env.truenas.example
nodes.summary: Template listing environment variables for deploying Travel Life to a TrueNAS Scale system, covering database, auth, geocoding, and optional third-party service settings.

nodes.name: CLAUDE.md
nodes.summary: Root project guidance file for Claude Code covering documentation index, tech stack, development commands, the mandatory build-and-deploy workflow, and environment setup conventions.
nodes.languageNotes: Written for consumption by an AI coding assistant; enforces a strict build/deploy procedure that must follow BUILD_AND_PUSH.md exactly.

nodes.name: DEPLOYMENT.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive production deployment guide covering Docker Compose and TrueNAS deployment options, environment configuration, database management, reverse proxy/SSL setup, backups, monitoring, and troubleshooting.

nodes.name: QUICK_START_PRODUCTION.md
nodes.summary: Condensed step-by-step guide for getting a production instance of Travel Life running quickly, from cloning the repo to running migrations and creating the first account.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Primary project README describing Travel Life's features, tech stack, setup instructions (Docker and local development), project structure, available scripts, external service configuration, and troubleshooting tips.

nodes.name: RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md
nodes.summary: Step-by-step checklist for releasing a new version of Travel Life, covering pre-release code quality/testing, version bumps, Docker builds, publishing images, git operations, and rollback procedures.

nodes.name: build.ps1
nodes.summary: PowerShell build script that loads .env.production and builds production-tagged backend and frontend Docker images for standard deployment.

nodes.name: build.sh
nodes.summary: Bash equivalent of build.ps1: loads .env.production and builds production-tagged backend and frontend Docker images using docker build.

nodes.name: build.truenas.ps1
nodes.summary: PowerShell build script that produces TrueNAS-tagged backend and frontend Docker images, using a TrueNAS-specific frontend Dockerfile with an nginx reverse proxy for /api and /uploads.

nodes.name: deploy-to-truenas.ps1
nodes.summary: Interactive PowerShell helper that deploys Travel Life to a TrueNAS host over SSH, offering three methods: copying only the compose file for pre-built images, copying full source for local build, or building and pushing images to a registry.

nodes.name: docker-compose.prod.yml
nodes.summary: Production Docker Compose stack defining PostGIS database, backend API, frontend, and self-hosted Nominatim services with healthchecks, restart policies, and environment-driven secrets for a standard (non-TrueNAS) production deployment.

nodes.name: docker-compose.truenas.optimized.yml
nodes.summary: Resource-optimized TrueNAS Docker Compose variant that drops the self-hosted Nominatim container in favor of the public OpenStreetMap Nominatim service and tunes PostgreSQL/container memory limits for lower idle resource usage.

nodes.name: docker-compose.truenas.yml
nodes.summary: TrueNAS Scale Docker Compose stack using pre-built GHCR images and bind mounts to TrueNAS datasets, with resource limits, healthchecks, and a self-hosted Nominatim geocoding service.
nodes.languageNotes: Contains hard-coded credentials and API keys in the example configuration, intended to be edited per-deployment rather than used verbatim.

nodes.name: docker-compose.yml
nodes.summary: Local development Docker Compose stack running PostGIS, the backend API (with hot reload via npm run dev), the Vite frontend dev server, and a self-hosted Nominatim geocoding service.

nodes.name: fix-journal-associations-migration.sql
nodes.summary: Manual SQL migration fallback for v1.2.0 that recreates the journal_activities, journal_lodgings, and journal_transportations join tables (with unique constraints and cascading foreign keys) when the automatic Prisma migration fails on TrueNAS.

nodes.name: journal_activities
nodes.summary: Join table linking journal entries to activities, with a unique (journal_id, activity_id) constraint and cascading foreign keys to journal_entries and activities.

nodes.name: journal_lodgings
nodes.summary: Join table linking journal entries to lodging records, with a unique (journal_id, lodging_id) constraint and cascading foreign keys to journal_entries and lodging.

nodes.name: journal_transportations
nodes.summary: Join table linking journal entries to transportation records, with a unique (journal_id, transportation_id) constraint and cascading foreign keys to journal_entries and transportation.

nodes.name: fix-migration.ps1
nodes.summary: PowerShell script to run on TrueNAS that fixes a failed Prisma migration (20251015_add_user_timezone) by conditionally adding the users.timezone column, marking the migration resolved, then deploying remaining migrations.

nodes.name: fix-migration.sh
nodes.summary: Bash equivalent of fix-migration.ps1, run inside the backend container to resolve the failed 20251015_add_user_timezone Prisma migration by applying the column change, marking the migration successful, and running prisma migrate deploy.

nodes.name: package.json
nodes.summary: Minimal root-level package.json declaring a single dependency on the claude-flow tooling package; not part of the frontend/backend application build pipeline.

nodes.name: release.ps1
nodes.summary: Automated PowerShell release script that bumps version numbers in backend/frontend package.json, verifies builds, commits the version bump, builds and pushes TrueNAS Docker images via build.truenas.ps1, and creates/pushes a git release tag, with dry-run and no-confirm modes.
nodes.languageNotes: Supports semantic version auto-increment (patch/minor/major) parsed from the current backend package.json version, plus small helper functions (Write-Step, Write-Success, etc.) for colored console output.
